title: Sharps Safety

references.label: Biosafety in Microbiological and Biomedical Laboratories (BMBL)

summary: Practices for safely handling and disposing of sharp items (needles, scalpels, broken glass, used slides) to prevent puncture/cut injuries and exposure.
explanation: Sharps present both an injury risk and, in a microbiology context, a potential exposure route if contaminated. Dedicated puncture-resistant sharps containers, located near the point of use, are the standard control, along with never recapping needles by hand.
keyPractices: Dispose of sharps immediately into a rigid, puncture-resistant, labeled sharps container.
Never recap a used needle by hand.
Never overfill a sharps container past its fill line.
Report any sharps injury immediately per institutional protocol.
commonMistakes: Leaving used slides/blades on the open bench instead of disposing of them immediately.
Attempting to force extra items into an already-full sharps container.
